title: The Elements of Behavior
coreMove: Diagnose any failed behavior by asking which of motivation, ability, or prompt was missing at the moment it should have happened, and fix that one.

exampleSpecs.domain: a night-shift nurse trying to drink more water during twelve-hour rotations
exampleSpecs.audience: a healthcare worker whose schedule wrecks ordinary routines
exampleSpecs.stakes: chronic dehydration headaches that bleed into patient handoffs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she traces her failed water-bottle habit to a missing prompt rather than weak willpower, and decides to redesign the cue instead of trying harder

exampleSpecs.domain: a retired electrician learning to take a daily blood-pressure reading at his kitchen counter
exampleSpecs.audience: an older adult navigating a new medical instruction
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether his cardiologist has data to adjust medication before his next appointment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the cuff sits in a drawer because nothing in his morning routine touches that drawer; the scene shows him moving it next to the coffee tin and a reading happening the next day

exampleSpecs.domain: a junior associate at a regional law firm trying to journal three lines before bed
exampleSpecs.stakes: a quiet sense that another self-improvement attempt is about to die
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she walks back through the week and identifies that motivation was high on Monday and gone by Thursday, and concludes the design was leaning on the wrong lever

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school orchestra teacher who keeps meaning to call his aging mother on Sunday afternoons
exampleSpecs.audience: an adult navigating family obligation alongside a busy week
exampleSpecs.stakes: the relationship slowly thinning into voicemails
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a conversation with a friend over coffee where he realizes the call has no anchor in his Sunday and is competing with everything else for attention

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance illustrator trying to stretch her wrists between commissions
exampleSpecs.audience: a self-employed creative whose day has no fixed structure
exampleSpecs.stakes: early signs of repetitive strain that could end her income
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the reader is asked to predict which of the three elements is failing, then the scene reveals it is ability — the stretch routine she chose takes eight minutes and she will not do eight minutes

exampleSpecs.domain: a line cook who wants to start reading non-cookbook books on the bus ride home
exampleSpecs.audience: a service-industry worker decompressing after a shift
exampleSpecs.stakes: a quiet aspiration to feel like a person with interests outside the kitchen
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he sits with the recognition that the bus ride is already an anchor and a prompt is already firing — what was missing was making the behavior small enough to start while still smelling like fryer oil
